facts.label: Sirva-se
facts.sub: O jeito simples de dizer ao convidado que ele pode pegar comida e bebida sem pedir.

facts.label: Dia do jogo
facts.sub: O Super Bowl costuma ser num domingo, no início de fevereiro. Em muitas casas, os amigos chegam antes do jogo, comem juntos e vestem a camisa do time preferido. Pergunte “Who’s playing?” se não conhece os times.

facts.label: Leve algo
facts.sub: Em festas de jogo, é comum o convidado levar um prato ou bebida para dividir, como salgadinhos ou refrigerante. Se o convite diz “Bring a snack”, leve algo simples. Anfitriões costumam dizer “Help yourself” e deixar tudo na mesa.

pages.title: My first Super Bowl party · 1/3
paragraphs: On Sunday, I went to a **Super Bowl party** in Dallas. My friend Claire has a big TV and a big couch. Many people came. Everyone wore a shirt of a favorite team.
Claire opened the door. “**Welcome to the party!**” she said. “**Thanks! Who’s playing?**” I asked. “The Chiefs and the Eagles,” she said. “**Who do you like?**” “**I like the Eagles.** Go Eagles!”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: My first Super Bowl party · 2/3
paragraphs: The kitchen smelled great. There were **wings**, chips and soda on the table. Claire’s brother Tom asked, “**Do you want some wings?**” “Yes, please,” I said. They were a little spicy, but very good. “**Help yourself**,” Tom said. “There is more.”

Soon Claire said, “**It’s game time!** Enjoy the game!” We sat on the couch and watched the TV. When a player ran to the end of the field, Claire shouted, “**Touchdown!**” Everyone cheered and clapped. It was like the movie Shaolin Soccer: two teams play, one team wins, and everybody has fun.

pages.title: My first Super Bowl party · 3/3
paragraphs: At halftime, we ate more and watched the commercials. Many people love the commercials as much as the game. My team lost, but I smiled. A good sport accepts the result.
At the end, the Eagles won. Claire was very happy. I went home tired and happy. I love Super Bowl parties.

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: No inglês falado, “do you” quase nunca soa separado: vira “dyuh”. Quem fala palavra por palavra soa lento e formal para os americanos.
pages.how: Junte o D com o “you” sem pausa: dyuh. Deixe a voz subir no final da pergunta e acentue WANT e WINGS: dyuh WAN-sum WINGS?
pages.tip: Treine com o rosto relaxado e a boca pouco aberta: palavras fracas são curtas e “moles”.
